audit.whatIsWrong: Null Sphere is called a silence in four places, including a whole 'why' row built on 'His Null Sphere silence prevents you from activating Q or W to escape'.
audit.why: Riot's current text for Null Sphere is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' No silence. The kit file's derived flag list carries silence as a tracked category and Kassadin has none — unlike the needsResearch topics, an absent tracked flag here is meaningful. This one matters practically: the text tells a Teemo he will be unable to press W and must therefore never be in Q range, which is a completely different (and much more passive) lane than the one he should actually play.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere does not silence. It interrupts channels and wraps him in a shield that absorbs magic damage — which, since all your damage is magic, is the real problem.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q description; kitFlags contains no silence)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'his only mobility is a short-range W hop'.
audit.why: Nether Blade (W) is an auto-attack empower that restores mana — 'Kassadin's next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage and restores Mana'. It is not a hop and it moves him nowhere. Before level 6 Kassadin has zero mobility of any kind, which is a much stronger statement in Teemo's favour than the one currently written.
audit.corrected: Kassadin has no mobility at all before Riftwalk. Nether Blade is an auto-attack reset and a mana battery.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'while Kassadin is still trying to carry 1v9 on a 50-second Riftwalk' and 'At two AP items Kassadin's Riftwalk cooldown collapses'.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds. It has never been a 50-second ability, and its cooldown does not 'collapse' at two items — it is already 2 seconds at rank 3. What actually limits him is the stacking mana cost: 'Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana.' Items give him the mana pool to pay that, which is a different thing to track and a different way to punish him.
audit.corrected: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 from the moment he hits 11. The stacking mana cost, not the cooldown, is what he buys his way out of.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is never explained, and the wants list tells Teemo to blind and shroom around him without any warning about it.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up, Kassadin can use Force Pulse.' Spells cast near him — including Teemo's own Blinding Dart, and mushrooms detonating beside him — charge his E. So the poke pattern the guide recommends is also the thing arming his only pre-6 damage window. That is the obscure interaction in this matchup and it is not written anywhere.
audit.corrected: Every spell cast near Kassadin charges Force Pulse, including your own Q. Poke with autos, not casts, when you are inside his 400-unit cone.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Void Stone halves your E poison magic damage' and elsewhere 'his passive shield absorbing the AP portion of every trade'.
audit.why: Riot gives no number: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' 'Halves' is invented. And the passive and the Q shield are two separate layers that the text keeps merging — the passive is flat magic damage reduction, the shield is a Null Sphere rider. Both stack against Teemo, whose damage is entirely magic; that stacking is worth stating precisely rather than fudging into one thing with a made-up percentage.
audit.corrected: Void Stone reduces magic damage taken (no published figure) and Null Sphere adds a magic-absorbing shield on top. Two separate layers, both aimed at you.

audit.why: 54.34% over 519 games is consistent with the FAVOURED framing and the pre-6 bully plan. No change.

edits.before: Kassadin's passive (Void Stone) halves your E poison magic damage and his Q silences you before you can kite — do not auto-trade in his face these first levels.
edits.after: Void Stone reduces all your magic damage and Null Sphere shields him against magic on top — Q does not silence, but those two layers gut your early poke.

edits.before: At two AP items Kassadin's Riftwalk cooldown collapses and he teleports through your shroom net freely — respect his burst and let your team close the game.
edits.after: Riftwalk is already 2s at rank 3 — what actually limits him is its stacking mana cost, so two AP items means he can chain blinks through your shroom net.

edits.before: Poke with E-coated autos from outside Q-silence range so Kassadin cannot silence-cancel your kite pattern
edits.after: Poke from outside his 650 Null Sphere range, and avoid casting beside him — nearby spells charge Force Pulse

edits.before: Null Sphere your Q so he can walk up safely and last-hit without eating a blind
edits.after: Open with Null Sphere for the magic shield, then farm safely through your poison

edits.before: His Null Sphere silence prevents you from activating Q or W to escape the moment it lands — at level 2 he can silence-cancel your kite and auto you back for more damage than his magic shield absorbs from your poke.
edits.after: Null Sphere does not silence you — it interrupts channels and wraps him in a shield that absorbs magic damage. That shield stacked on Void Stone is what blanks your poison at level 2, not any lockdown.

edits.before: With Q max-ranked your blind is reliable and your shroom radius expanding, but Kassadin still has his passive shield absorbing the AP portion of every trade — the lane is still genuinely contested and neither side can force a clean kill.
edits.after: With Q max-ranked your blind is reliable and your shroom radius expanding, but Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield still eat the magic half of every trade — the lane stays contested and neither side forces a clean kill.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 champions in the game, but his Void Stone passive eats a huge chunk of your E poison magic damage the moment he walks up — do not rely on short poison trades to chunk him down the way you would versus a Darius. Instead, weave physical auto-poke from maximum range between minions, and never stand close enough for his Q silence to land: if he Null Spheres you, you cannot W away before he closes. At level 2 he gains Nether Blade and a mana-restore loop on minions, meaning he can sustain through small poke indefinitely if you let him farm in peace — keep him off the wave with auto harassment, not poison-stacking, and accept that you will not burst him before the wave crashes.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 champions in the game, but Void Stone eats a chunk of your Toxic Shot magic damage the moment he walks up — do not expect short poison trades to chunk him the way they would a Darius. Weave auto-poke from maximum range between minions and stay outside his 650-unit Null Sphere: it does not silence you, whatever you have read, but it shields him against exactly the damage you deal. Be careful casting near him at all — every spell cast in his vicinity charges Force Pulse. At level 2 he gains Nether Blade, an auto-attack empower that also restores mana off minions, so he can sustain through small poke indefinitely if you let him farm in peace. Keep him off the wave with auto harassment, not poison-stacking.

edits.before: From levels 4-5 your Q reaches max rank and the matchup opens up considerably: Kassadin still has no dash, his only mobility is a short-range W hop, and his magic shield does nothing against your Q blind. Time your trades around his Null Sphere cooldown — when it is down, walk up, auto him twice to proc E poison, fire Q-blind, then W away before he can respond. Plant Noxious Traps at the tribush and river brush entrances at level 6: every Riftwalk he throws toward you has to land somewhere, and if that somewhere is a shroom he takes damage, gets slowed, and you re-establish range. The level 6 spike is yours precisely because your map layer goes up the moment his ult goes up — use it.
edits.after: From levels 4-5 the matchup opens up considerably, and for a better reason than the one usually given: Kassadin has no mobility at all until 6. Nether Blade is an auto-attack empower, not a hop, so before Riftwalk there is genuinely nothing he can do about a Teemo who holds spacing. Time your trades around Null Sphere — 9s at rank 1, 7s at rank 5 — because that shield is what absorbs your poison. When it is spent, walk up, auto him twice to lay Toxic Shot, blind, then W away. Plant Noxious Traps at the tribush and river entrances at level 6: every Riftwalk has to land somewhere, and if that somewhere is a shroom he takes damage, gets slowed, and you re-establish range. Your level 6 spike arrives the same moment his does — use it.

edits.before: At two items Kassadin's Riftwalk cooldown drops low enough that he can chain three blinks through your mushroom net before any of them proc twice, and a single Everfrost or Shadowflame combo at that point exceeds your HP pool. Your job is no longer to duel him — it is to keep your mushroom perimeter intact around any objective or tower fight so his team cannot ignore your split pressure, and to never be caught alone in a bush he has not seen you enter. Your lead from the early poke window should already be a completed item or two towers; if it is, your team closes while Kassadin is still trying to carry 1v9 on a 50-second Riftwalk.
edits.after: At two items Kassadin can chain Riftwalks through your mushroom net — the cooldown was already 2 seconds at rank 3, so what the items really buy him is the mana to pay its stacking cost — and a single Everfrost or Shadowflame combo at that point exceeds your HP pool. Your job is no longer to duel him: keep your mushroom perimeter intact around any objective or tower fight so his team cannot ignore your split pressure, and never be caught alone in a bush he has not seen you enter. Your lead from the early poke window should already be a completed item or two towers; if it is, your team closes while he is still hunting for a 1v9.

edits.before: Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely. Only take the trade when Kassadin's Riftwalk is down.
edits.after: Blind erases his Nether Blade auto, but Null Sphere shields the magic you trade back. Keep trades shallow.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3; its stacking mana cost is the real limit. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: The invented Null Sphere silence was the worst error in my slice — it appeared in the spikes, the early text and a whys row, and it changes how the entire pre-6 lane is played. Riot's current description has no silence and the kit file carries no silence flag (and silence is one of the flags the kit builder tracks, so its absence is informative rather than unknown). Worth grepping the rest of the repo for 'Null Sphere silence'.
